question.prompt: Let \(S(n)\) equal the sum of the digits of positive integer \(n.\) For example, \(S(1507)=13.\) For a particular positive integer \(n,\) \(S(n)=1274.\) Which of the following could be the value of \(S(n+1)?\)

solutions.title: Track the carries
solutions.explanation:
The change in digit sum depends on how many 9s occur at the end of \(n\). If there are exactly \(k\) trailing 9s, adding 1 turns them into zeros and increases the preceding digit by 1. Therefore
\[
S(n+1)=S(n)+1-9k=1275-9k.
\]
Thus \(S(n+1)\) must have remainder 6 when divided by 9. The choices \(1,3,12,1239,1265\) have remainders \(1,3,3,6,5\), respectively, so only \(1239\) qualifies.

To verify that it can occur, take \(n\) to consist of 1238 ones followed by four 9s. Then
\[
S(n)=1238+4\cdot9=1274.
\]
Adding 1 changes the ending \(19999\) to \(20000\), leaving 1237 ones before it. Hence
\[
S(n+1)=1237+2=\boxed{1239}.
\]
The answer is D.
